<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Neutron imaging is a fundamental technique for the study of light elements, indispensable for the study of lithium distribution in batteries, water dynamics in soil or hydrogen storage in materials. Its quantitative accuracy is limited by the presence of scattered neutrons at the detector, which reduces the image contrast and introduces systematic errors in the attenuation coefficient evaluation. Here we present a dual detector setup to correct the neutron scatter component. The first detector, placed close to the sample, captures the transmitted and scattered neutrons while the second, installed downstream, captures mostly transmitted neutrons, with the scattered neutrons strongly suppressed by distance. By combining both acquisitions, we obtain a scatter-free radiography with the superior resolution of the first detector, without any sample-dependent calibration. This method is validated on a standard resolution sample to assess that there is no degradation in image quality; and the performance is proven on a highly challenging 4D tomography experiment using H
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$_2$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    O and D
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$_2$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    O mixtures within a heterogeneous soil matrix. This method brings neutron tomography from a qualitative visualisation technique to a quantitative analysis of heterogeneous, dynamic systems containing strong scattering substances.
                  </jats:p>
title: Material calibration-independent neutron scattering corrections for quantitative imaging

metadata.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate characterization of ion beams from sub-MeV to multi-MeV energies is essential for diagnostics in laser-driven ion acceleration and fusion research. CR-39 detectors are widely used to measure absolute ion yields, while ion energy and incidence angle can be inferred from etched-pit geometries. In this study, we present an automated CR-39 pit detection method that enables reliable extraction of pit geometries from two-dimensional optical micrographs, with improved discrimination of overlapping pits under high-flux conditions. This capability enables reliable analysis in high-density regimes where conventional methods are limited by significant track overlap. By integrating the detected pit shapes with a pit-formation model based on Monte Carlo simulations of restricted energy loss, energy and angular characterization of laser-driven proton beams is achieved with enhanced precision and computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides a robust and scalable approach for automated CR-39 analysis and is applicable to a broad range of ion-beam diagnostics and spectroscopy.</jats:p>
title: Automated CR-39 pit detection for energy and angular characterization of laser-driven ion beams
